common_name: Bounce Pink Flame Impatiens (Downy-Mildew-Resistant Sun-Tolerant Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into partial shade to partial sun in fertile, well-drained soil; Bounce Pink Flame is a downy-mildew-resistant impatiens hybrid bred to replace traditional Impatiens walleriana in beds where the disease has been a problem.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to partial sun, and feed and water regularly to keep the vigorous, well-branched mounds blooming without interruption. Bounce Pink Flame is a vegetatively propagated interspecific impatiens hybrid bred with resistance to impatiens downy mildew, covering its mounded habit in bright rose-pink flowers with a slightly deeper center from spring through frost. It rebounds quickly after a rain or an accidental broken stem, springing back into full, tidy bloom within days, a trait that gave the series its name. Give it more consistent moisture than SunPatiens types, since Bounce is bred primarily for shade and part-sun performance rather than full-sun heat tolerance, and pinch leggy stems in midsummer to keep plantings dense.
sources: Selecta One — Bounce Impatiens series notes

common_name: Rockapulco Pink Impatiens (Fully Double Rose-Bud Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant purchased transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade to full shade. Rockapulco is a Proven Winners series bred for fully double, rose-bud-like flowers and improved heat and humidity tolerance compared to older double impatiens strains.

directions: Plant in partial to full shade in moist, well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic soil; Rockapulco Pink is a Proven Winners impatiens bred for fully double, ruffled, rose-like pink blooms that resemble small roses more than a typical five-petaled impatiens flower, held over a compact, mounding plant that continues flowering non-stop from spring through frost in deep shade where few other bedding annuals bloom well at all. Like other Impatiens walleriana selections it remains susceptible to impatiens downy mildew, the fungal disease that has caused serious losses in impatiens plantings across North America since 2011; provide good air circulation, avoid overhead watering, and consider New Guinea impatiens or SunPatiens in areas with a known history of the disease. Deadheading is not required since spent blooms drop cleanly on their own.

common_name: SunPatiens Compact Lilac Impatiens (Sun-Tolerant Season-Long Bedding Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; unlike traditional impatiens, SunPatiens tolerates full sun and heat without wilting and is also resistant to downy mildew, the disease that has devastated standard impatiens plantings.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, and feed regularly through the season to sustain the vigorous growth and nonstop bloom this series is bred for. SunPatiens Compact Lilac is a vegetatively propagated, downy-mildew-resistant impatiens hybrid bred to tolerate full sun and heat that would scorch or collapse traditional Impatiens walleriana, holding a dense, well-branched, self-cleaning mound covered in soft lilac-purple flowers from spring through frost. The Compact series stays more tidy and controlled than the larger Vigorous SunPatiens line, making it well suited to smaller beds, borders, and container plantings where a large spreading mound would be too much. Consistent moisture is important during establishment and through the hottest stretch of summer, though established plantings tolerate brief dry spells better than traditional impatiens.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Bedding Plant Trials

common_name: SunPatiens Vigorous Salmon New Guinea Impatiens (Large Vase-Habit Downy-Mildew-Resistant Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; SunPatiens Vigorous Salmon is the large-form, vase-habit tier of the SunPatiens line, reaching 30-36 inches, with strong resistance to downy mildew.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, watering regularly to keep soil consistently moist. SunPatiens Vigorous Salmon is the largest-growing tier of the SunPatiens breeding line, forming a substantial, upright, vase-shaped plant 30 to 36 inches tall covered in warm salmon-orange flowers from spring through frost, a dramatically bigger scale than the compact, mounding SunPatiens forms bred for smaller beds and containers. Like the rest of the SunPatiens line, it carries strong resistance to the downy mildew that devastated old-fashioned impatiens walleriana plantings, and tolerates considerably more sun than traditional shade impatiens while still performing well in partial shade. Its size makes it useful as a substantial seasonal hedge, back-of-border filler, or large container centerpiece. No deadheading is needed to keep it blooming continuously.
